Subject: POC runtime readiness & traffic specs — next steps for NovaRetail

Hi Ellen / Samir —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up the trial environment and the acceptance criteria. Please flag anything I got wrong.

Recap of workloads discussed:
- Autocomplete (search): very short queries, frequent; low token length per request.
- Document summarization: long documents, higher token lengths, lower RPS but heavier per-request cost.
- Mixed API: occasional reranking and embedding calls (background batch jobs).

Traffic profile we heard from your team (please confirm):
- Aggregate target sustained RPS for POC: ~75 RPS across services (peak bursts up to ~225 RPS for 3-4 minutes during campaigns).
- Per-workload breakdown (approx):
  - Autocomplete: steady 150 RPS at peak, median token length 10–18 tokens.
  - Summarization: peak 12–18 RPS, median request size ~420 tokens, 95th percentile up to ~1,100 tokens.
  - Reranking/batch: ~2–4 concurrent jobs, each sending batched lists of 32–128 items.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrent requests 10–35, burst concurrency up to ~220.
- Token distribution: average request ~160 tokens, median ~80, p95 ~900 tokens (summarization dominates).

Proposed success criteria (POC acceptance):
- Functional: accuracy/sanity checks against your reference prompt set (we'll use the seed prompts you provide).
- Performance: p95 latency for autocomplete < 200ms; p95 latency for summarization < 1.2s at steady target; system remains within error budget during 3x burst window.
- Stability: no crashes or memory errors during a 24-hour soak at sustained target load with two 10-minute stress ramps.
- Cost profile: token-unit cost estimate within your forecasted threshold (we'll provide a pre- and post-POC cost projection).

Immediate next steps / owners:
- NOVARETAIL: share sample payloads (JSONL with representative query/response pairs) and a prioritized prompt set — Ellen / Samir — by EOD Friday.
- REDWOOD: provision pilot cluster and run an initial load bench — Karthik (infra) — within 48 hours of receiving payloads.
- REDWOOD: define canary success run and measurement dashboard — Kimberly (customer success).
- Schedule: target POC kickoff window: week of 7 June 2027, nominal duration 4 weeks.

Attachments: sample payload template and security matrix attached to this thread.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff slot once we have the payloads.

—
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@novaretail.com>

Subject: Re: POC runtime readiness & traffic specs — next steps for NovaRetail

Thanks Kimberly — this is a very clear recap. Confirming items from our side and adding detail so your infra team can size the pilot properly.

Confirmed workload numbers (we captured more granular splits):
- Autocomplete/search:
  - Typical query tokens: 8–20 (median 12).
  - Peak observed RPS during promotions: 180 RPS for 2–5 minutes; baseline 40–60 RPS.
- Summarization:
  - Document sizes: 2,000–15,000 characters; after tokenization ~350–1,200 tokens.
  - Expected peak RPS: 12–18 (as you noted).
- Reranking/embeddings (background): batched embeddings 128 items every minute during nightly aggregation windows.
- Concurrency: normal 15–30; isolated spikes up to 250 concurrent open sockets when a marketing campaign triggers heavy autocomplete.

POC timeline constraints:
- We are available to start the POC week of 7 June; preferred end date is no later than 2 July (4 weeks).
- Key internal reviewers: Samir (platform), Li Chen (security) — CC'ing Samir; I will add Li later to security thread.

Files: attached a 500-line sample_payloads.jsonl (subset) and our security matrix (redacted). We will provide a fuller dataset next business day.

Can you confirm the target cluster sizing and whether you can simulate the 5-minute 3x burst pattern during the canary? We want the canary to include at least two artificial bursts to validate autoscaling and latency SLAs.

—
Ellen Park
Senior Product Manager, Search & Personalization
NovaRetail

Ellen / Samir —

Thanks for the clarifications and the sample payload subset — that helps a lot. Short technical plan and owners below.

Technical plan (high level):
- Provisioning: we will allocate a dedicated pilot pool for NovaRetail with 2 GPU nodes (pilot nodes) and a mix of autoscaling workers for burst capacity. The pilot will be isolated from other customers.
- Canary + stress: run a staged canary that includes:
  1) functional canary (low volume) to validate correctness against your prompt set,
  2) steady-state throughput run at the target sustained RPS for 6 hours,
  3) two injected burst windows (3–5 minutes each) at 3x baseline to validate autoscaler and latency.
- Measurements: token-level cost breakdown, per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, queue lengths. We will export dashboards and a CSV summary at the end of each run.
- Telemetry: tracing, event logs, and per-request metadata (prompt hash, token counts) — we will need your sample payloads annotated if you want the full mapping.

Owners and timelines:
- infra & perf lead: Karthik Iyer — provisioning and load runs (owner for pilot cluster).
- account & commercial lead: Aditya Rao — deal coordination, procurement, credits.
- customer success: Kimberly Park — acceptance criteria, dashboard signoff, final readout.

Deliverables and dates (tentative):
- Pilot provisioned and ready for dry-run: 2027-06-08 (48–72 hrs after full payload set).
- Canary + performance run: 2027-06-09 through 2027-06-10.
- 24-hour soak and final readout: 2027-06-16.

Action items for NovaRetail:
- Provide full sample payloads with token counts annotated (JSONL) and any disallowed prompt patterns.
- Confirm the two surge windows you want us to simulate (UTC times).

We can adjust node counts if the initial runs show under-provisioning; Karthik will report hourly during the canary.

Regards,
Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
